prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: I had walked / for most of the day / to Kanpur and then / got on the train to Mumbai.
options: got on the train to Mumbai
explanation: Two successive past actions joined by 'and then' both take the simple past, so 'I had walked' should be 'I walked'; the past perfect is unnecessary when the sequence is already clear.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: This is a worst famine this country has seen in a decade.
explanation: A superlative identifying a unique instance takes the definite article: 'This is the worst famine this country has seen in a decade.'

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Between Raima and Saima, (a) / the former is intelligent, (b) / while latter is beautiful. (c) / No error (d)
explanation: 'Former' and 'latter' always take 'the', so 'while latter is beautiful' should be 'while the latter is beautiful'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: This is most beautiful / thing I have ever / seen in my life.
explanation: The superlative needs the definite article: 'This is the most beautiful thing I have ever seen in my life.'

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: How many languages do / most children / in India know?
explanation: No error: 'most children' correctly means 'the majority of children' without an article, and the interrogative structure 'How many languages do ... know?' is proper.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: It is commonly believed / that Democracy is / a best form / of the government.
explanation: A superlative adjective takes the definite article, so 'a best form' must be 'the best form'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The harder / you work, / better / it will be.
explanation: In the double comparative construction 'the more... the more', both comparatives need 'the'; 'better' should be 'the better'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Fashion might not be first / thing that comes to mind when / we think of isolation strategies.
options: thing that comes to mind when
explanation: 'First' as an ordinal needs the definite article, so 'might not be first thing' should be 'might not be the first thing'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: A grand celebration / in honour of / a first woman gold medallist / was organised by the family members.
explanation: The ordinal 'first' requires the definite article: 'the first woman gold medallist', not 'a first woman gold medallist'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: This is first time / I have eaten such / a tasty cake.
explanation: The ordinal needs 'the': 'This is the first time I have eaten such a tasty cake.'

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: He has been suffering from (A) / the measles for the past (B) / two consecutive weeks. (C) / No Error (D)
explanation: Names of diseases like measles, mumps and diabetes take no article, so 'the measles' should simply be 'measles'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The sun rises in east (A) / and sets in the west, (B) / maintaining a perfect celestial rhythm. (C) / No Error (D)
explanation: Unique directions take the definite article, so it should be 'rises in the east' to match 'sets in the west'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error. The article that she wrote / for the last week's Sunday Supplement / fairly criticises / the abuse of mobile phones.
options: for the last week’s Sunday Supplement
explanation: With a possessive time expression like 'last week's', no article is used: 'for last week's Sunday Supplement'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: After knowing truth, / the jury took the right decision / in the case.
options: The jury took the right decision

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: Anti-party activities / improved my relations /with an opposition.

explanation: The restaurant has already been specified, so the definite article is required: 'the interior of the restaurant'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Deepak is studying B.tech. at IIT Delhi to become the engineer.
explanation: A profession mentioned generally takes the indefinite article: 'to become an engineer', not 'the engineer'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I have the hundred reasons to not attend the meeting tomorrow.
explanation: Numbers like hundred take 'a' in such expressions: 'a hundred reasons', not 'the hundred reasons'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The library provides access to (1)/ extensive collection of journals (2)/ and research databases (3)/ for postgraduate scholars. (4)/

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options. If there is no error, select No error.
sentence: What is the function of the kidney in the body?

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Whole country applauded the courage of our soldiers.

Washington Irving’s writing career started at

options: I have a dog and a cow

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: They will not attend / the event / as they’re going / away at end of April.
